data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's covering principle for distinguishing genuine reliability from lucky compliance is logically self-undermining: it demands evidence that the checklist overturned a 'wrong intuition,' but its own countercondition admits cases where no wrong intuition is ever formed (because the checklist is comprehensive or members lack intuition). In exactly those cases the demanded evidence is absent, yet SRC_001's falsification rule says the absence of error-correction trajectory means mere procedural illusion — so a genuinely reliable comprehensive checklist would be misclassified as mere compliance.
